Once there was a little girl named Alice. She was three years old and loved to go visit her family. One day, she went to visit her aunt's house with her mom. 

When they arrived, Alice couldn't help but noticed the big house. She had never been there before and it was full of unknown things. Her mom asked her to go upstairs to look for the toilet. 

Alice went up the stairs, but she was scared! Before she knew it, she was standing in front of a small room. She poked her head inside and what do you think she saw? The toilet! 

Alice smiled and shivered with joy. She quickly ran back to her mom and said, "I found the toilet!" Her mom was so proud of her. 

Alice came to visit her aunt's house many times in the future and she was never afraid of the unknown again.

The day was hot, and Emily was thirsty. She looked around for something to drink, but there was nothing. 

Then, she got an idea. She ran to her bedroom and grabbed the sheet from her bed. She yelled, â€œMommy, Iâ€™m thirsty! Can I drink the sheet?" 

Mommy smiled and said, "No, Emilly, but I have something even better. Come downstairs and I'll show you." 

Emily ran downstairs and found a big, dependable bowl of water. Excitedly, she asked, "Is this what I get to drink?" 

Mommy nodded and said, "Yes! This is what you will drink!"

Emily smiled and happily drank the cool water. She was so happy that she had a dependable source of water when she was thirsty!

The day was warm and the sun was shining. The sky was big and blue.

John and his mommy went outside. John was three years old and he LOVED to explore. 

"Look," said John, pointing to a hose that was laying on the ground. "What's that?"

"It's a hose," said his mommy. "We can use it to water the plants in the garden."

John grabbed the hose and ran around the garden. He noticed how cool the water felt as it sprayed him.

John's mommy laughed. "Let's sit down and cool off," she said. 

John and his mommy sat down in the shade. The cool air felt good on their skin. They watched the water from the hose sparkle in the sun.

John gave a big smile. He was happy to spend the day outside with his mommy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Penny, and she had the most amazing imagination! Penny loved to design things and today she wanted to design a shade for the garden.

Penny looked at the garden and said, "This is so important! I need to make the perfect shade". She thought for a moment, and then started getting some materials together.

Penny's mom saw her determined little face and asked her what she was doing. "I'm designing a shade for the garden, Mom! What do you think?" Penny replied. 

Her mom smiled and said, "That sounds like a great idea Penny. You need to make sure that it can protect all the plants from the sun!"

And so, with her mom's help, Penny got to work creating the perfect shade for the garden. When it was all done, everyone was so impressed! It was a perfect addition to the garden, and most importantly, it provided just the right amount of shade.

Once upon a time there were two friends Mo and Bob. Mo was very independent and Bob was very dependent. One day, Mo asked Bob if he could help him make dinner. Bob said no because he wanted to do things on his own. 

Mo got angry and decided to make dinner without Bob. He boiled some potatoes and put them on the table. When Bob went to the kitchen, he saw the potatoes and asked Mo why he hadn't served them. 

Mo replied â€œYou don't need help. You're independent. You can serve yourself.â€ Bob felt sad and started crying. 

Mo realized that independence isn't always something to brag about. Everyone needs help sometimes. The moral of this story is that it's ok to ask for help when you need it.

Once there was a little girl named Linny. She loved to play in the park and one day when she was there, she saw a boy, who she never saw before. His name was Mike.

Linny was so excited to make a new friend that she ran up to him and said, "Hi Mike! Wanna play?"
 Mike said, "Yes, let's play!" 

So, they both went to the swings and started to swing. The higher Linny swung, the more she laughed and smiled. However, Mike kept going higher and higher until he fell off the swing and hurt his arm. 

Linny ran over to Mike and asked if he was ok. He said, "No, my arm really hurts," while he was crying. Linny wanted to make him feel better, so she said, "I have a yummy muffin in my bag. Maybe that will help." 

Mike smiled as he ate the muffin. His arm still hurt, but he was happy that he had a new friend. They both continued to play in the park and had lots of fun.

Once there was a blue bird. He lived in a big palm tree by the beach. Everyday he would take naps in the branches of the palm tree and look at the beautiful blue sky and the sparkling ocean.

One day, the bird decided to take a little adventure and explore the beach beneath his tree. He flew around the shoreline and saw a small fish swimming in a shallow pool of water. He watched in awe as the fish swam around in the water.

But just as the bird was about to land, he noticed something that worried him. The fish had started to rot and it made him sad. He flew away in a hurry, but the awful smell followed the bird.

He quickly returned to his palm tree, and was frightened yet again by an even bigger rotting fish lying beneath the branches. He feared the beach was all rotting and he would never be able to rest in the branches of his beloved tree again.

The blue bird sadly flew off, away from the rotten beach. Sad, he was never able to visit his beloved palm tree and the beach again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Annie. She was only three, but she was very brave. One day, she decided to go to the museum. As she stepped inside, she felt a little troubled.

Annie started to search around the museum. She looked at the ancient paintings and the beautiful sculptures. She saw a shiny dinosaur statue and a huge globe, too.

Suddenly, Annie heard a noise. "Who's there?" she said in a loud voice.

A wise old professor popped out from behind a corner. "Hello, young one. What are you searching for?"

Annie smiled. "I'm looking for something special," she said.

The professor smiled back. "Ah, I believe I know what it is. Follow me!"

Annie and the professor went to the far end of the museum and he opened a secret door. Inside was a room full of amazing treasures! Annie smiled. Her troubles had gone away. From that day on, she visited the museum often, searching for more special surprises.

Once upon a time there was a big old tree. It was so big that it touched the clouds. Every day lots of birds and animals came to the tree and they all supported each other.

One day a little mouse called Sally decided to climb the tree. She kept going higher and higher and soon she was so high that she could see the whole world. Then she heard a loud noise and quickly climbed down.

When Sally got back to the ground she saw a bright yellow bulldozer. An old man with big glasses was driving the bulldozer and wanted to cut the tree down.

Sally shook her head and shouted, "No! This tree supports us all. You can't cut it down!"

The old man looked surprised and smiled at Sally, "You are right my little friend. I'm so sorry."

Sally smiled and the old man turned his bulldozer away. The animals, birds and everyone else cheered for Sally and thanked her for protecting their big old tree.

The sun shined bright in the sky and Jack felt its heat on his face. He was excited for today. He was going to visit the farm with his mom.

They went to the barn and got a basket of vegetables. Jack liked the carrots best. He took a carrot out of the basket and felt its crunch in his hand. He was so happy that he hopped up and down.

When they were getting ready to leave, Jack noticed something on the ground. â€œWhatâ€™s that, mom?â€ asked Jack.

His mom smiled and answered, â€œThatâ€™s a chili pepper. Itâ€™s spicy,â€ she said.

Jack was scared. He had never seen a chili pepper before and his stomach was starting to tremble.

His mom reassured him. â€œDonâ€™t be scared, Jack. You can hold my hand,â€ she said.

So, Jack reached out with his tiny hand and held his momâ€™s hand. With courage, he picked up the chili pepper and the spicy aroma filled the farm.

Jack smiled. He realized there was nothing to be afraid of.

Once there was a ship named Little Birdy. Little Birdy was harmless and sailed through the ocean without causing any harm.

One day, Little Birdy met another ship in the middle of the ocean. The other ship was called Big Bob. Big Bob asked Little Birdy if he wanted to race. Little Birdy replied, "Yes I do!"

So the ships started their race. Little Birdy was very fast and soon caught up with Big Bob. Big Bob shouted, "Faster! Faster!" Little Birdy flew through the ocean faster and faster.

Soon, Little Birdy had passed Big Bob and won the race. Big Bob was so surprised that he yelled, "Will you teach me how you can go so fast in the ocean?"

Little Birdy smiled and said, "All you have to do is sail with a harmless heart!"

Tommy had a new bucket of paints and a brush. He looked out on the landscape in front of him and saw something ugly - the sky was dull and grey. 

Tommy grabbed his brush and started to mix new colours in his bucket. He smiled as he created bands of orange, yellow and pink. 

Suddenly, Tommy heard a voice behind him.

"Wow - what are you making?" asked Tommy's mom. Tommy grinned and held up his brush.

"I'm making a beautiful landscape," he said. "I'm putting lots of colourful paint on it to make it look nice." 

Tommy's mom smiled. "That's wonderful," she said. "See how different your painting looks now compared to the dull landscape before?"

Tommy nodded. He was proud of the beautiful painting he had made.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Emma. Every day she would go jogging in the park. One day, she was playing in the park and she forgot to bring her shoes. Emma didn't want to jog in her socks, so she stayed in one spot and watched all of the other people running and jogging in the park.

Then, all of a sudden, something strange happened. The ground began to shake, and the shaking got more and more violent. Emma screamed in fear and was glad when the shaking stopped.

When it stopped, Emma looked around. The ground was all covered in broken branches, dirt and leaves. She looked up and saw a giant tree that had fallen to the ground. Emma's heart leapt into her throat.

The giant tree had ripped out a large chunk of the grassy ground. What was worse, it had uncovered a big, nasty, slimy puddle of muddy water. The water tasted bitter, and it smelled bad, too.

Suddenly, Emma heard someone speak. It was an old man who lived near the park. "That's why you should always bring your shoes with you," he said, "you never know when the ground will shake like that."

Jill and Jack were brother and sister. They always liked to quarrel. Today was no exception. "I want to play with your toy!" shouted Jill. "No! It's mine!" shouted Jack.

Just then their mom came in. "What's going on here?" she asked. "Jill and I are quarreling" said Jack. "Well, why don't you both do some yoga instead?" said their mom. So, Jill and Jack did some yoga together. They did the tree pose and the warrior pose.

After yoga, Jill and Jack were tired. But they were also happy. They had stopped quarreling. To celebrate, their mom took them to the store. "We can buy something nice but it has to be cheap!" said mom. So they each got a small toy. And they were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a kind boy called Jack. He liked to play in the garden, and laugh with his friends.

One day, Jack was in the garden, looking for a flower when he saw a butterfly. It was quick, and it flew around in circles. Jack wanted to catch it, but he couldn't reach it. He tried and tried, but he only made it more scared. 

Suddenly, out of nowhere, a frog hopped up to Jack and spoke. "Why don't you strike the butterfly?" Jack was amazed and asked, "Why?" The frog said, "It's harmless, so you won't hurt it." 

Jack thought that this was a good idea so he tried it out. He reached in with his hands, and struck the butterfly softly. Suddenly, the butterfly landed in his hands. Jack was happy, and couldn't believe it! He had caught the butterfly!

Andi was walking to the restaurant. She was feeling excited because she was going out to dinner with her family. When they arrived at the restaurant, they were very surprised.

Andi peeked inside and saw all the delicious food. Her eyes twinkled with excitement. Every dish smelled so appealing.

Andi's brother, Ben, was standing next to her. He was feeling jealous because Andi was so excited. He said to Andi, "Why do you get to go inside? I want to go in too!"

Andi replied, "I am sorry, Ben. You can look, but not go in. We have to wait for Mom and Dad!"

Ben pouted and said, "That's not fair!" But he was still excited to peek inside the restaurant. So, he grinned and said, "Let me see what's inside!"

Andi and Ben looked eagerly through the windows. They could see all the people inside, laughing and enjoying their meal. Ben was so jealous he couldn't wait to have dinner too. 

Finally, Mom and Dad arrived and they went into the restaurant to have dinner.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. He was out playing with his friends in the park when he saw a big, red brick. He wanted to have the brick, so he hopped off his swing and ran to get it.

But when he got there, Jack realized he couldn't pick up the brick â€“ it was too heavy! He started to yell for help, but no one heard him.

Just then, a brilliant girl walked by. Her name was Lucy. She saw Jack trying to pick up the brick and came over to help him. She said to him, "I can lift that brick for you. No problem!"

Jack said, "Thank you!" He was embarrassed that he couldn't pick up the brick, but was so glad Lucy was there to help him. She easily lifted the brick, handed it to Jack, and walked away with a smile.

Jack was so happy. He picked up the brick and ran to show his friends. He had a brilliant plan all along â€“ they were going to have a brick race!

Once upon a time there lived an old mule. He was very poor, living all alone in a small shed without anything to eat or drink. The mule's belly rumbled and ached from hunger. He was so poor that he had no one to help him.

One day, a little girl with curly hair walking by the mule's shed noticed him. She called out, "Hello Mr Mule, why do you look so sad?" The mule replied sadly, "I am so poor I have nothing to eat".

The little girl felt sorry for the poor mule. She said, "Don't worry, help will arrive soon!"

The little girl ran off and the mule thought to himself, 'How can a poor mule like me ever get help?'

The next day, the little girl returned with a big bag full of food. She said, "See, here is all the food you need! Now you can get better!" The mule was full of joy and happiness.

The mule thanked the little girl and said, "You have helped me get out of this situation. I am forever grateful."

The little girl smiled, hugged the mule, and said, "You'll never be poor again!"

One day, a little girl named Ava decided to start her own garden. She was so excited to improve her garden. She dug the soil and planted lots of different flowers.

She watered the plants every day and waited for them to grow. Finally, two weeks later, the flowers started to blossom. 

Ava was so proud of her work. She asked her mother to come outside and take a look. Ava said, "I improved this garden by myself!"

Her mother was very impressed. She said, "I'm so proud of you Ava. You worked really hard ".

But as the months passed, something strange started happening. The flowers had a very bitter taste.

Ava was sad. She thought to herself, "perhaps I need to improve the soil to make the flowers taste better".

So she started to research better ways to improve her garden. After a few months she found the right solution and added some soil amendments to make the flowers taste sweet. 

After a few short weeks, the flowers started to taste much better. Ava was happy again and she sang with joy. Her garden continued to improve and she was so proud of her hard work!

Once upon a time, there was a gray fish who lived in the sea. Her name was Jelly. One day, Jelly got a silly idea. She wanted to see what it was like to live on land.

Jelly swam up to the shore and peered out of the water. A little boy was playing in the sand. The little boy saw Jelly and ran to get his mommy.

"Mommy, mommy," the little boy said, "look at the gray fish!" His mommy smiled and said, "That's a jellyfish, and she looks like she might be trying to come up to the beach. Let's help her."

The little boy and his mommy put their hands in the water and gently guided Jelly onto the sand. Jelly was so happy she did a little dance. They both laughed and Jelly thanked them for their help.

"Would you like to come inside, Jelly?" The little boy's mommy asked. Jelly nodded her head and was taken inside the house. 

Once inside, the little boy and his mommy made Jelly feel welcome. They showed her every room and every toy they had. Jelly was amazed at all the things they included in their home! But the best part was when they took her out to the back yard and showed her the big swimming pool.

Jelly was so excited she could hardly contain herself! She jumped right in and started to swim

Paula was a very intelligent and curious three year old girl. She loved to explore the world around her, especially when she and her family went for walks through the neighbourhood park. On this particular day, Paula noticed a wagon near the playground. She asked her dad what it was and he told her it was a special wagon just for her!

Paula was so excited and she quickly ran over to the wagon, jumping inside. Her dad smiled and started pushing her around the park. Every time she came across something new, she asked her dad what it was and he patiently answered all her questions.

As they neared the end of the park, Paula noticed something moving in the bushes. It was a crow, chirping and hopping around. Paula thought this was the most exciting thing she'd seen all day and so her dad explained that the crow was searching for food.

Paula had a feeling this was going to be the beginning of something special. She couldn't quite put her finger on it, but as they continued walking, more and more crows started appearing around them. Soon enough, Paula noticed a huge flock of crows following behind the wagon! She was so thrilled to have made this intelligent discovery.

Once there was a little girl called Mia who was three years old. She was excited to go to the beach with her Mummy and Daddy. When they arrived, they put down their towel and Mia explored the beach. She saw some little fishes swimming in the sea.

Mia's Mummy said, "Mia, do you want to swim too?"
Mia got very excited and ran to the sea. 

Mummy gave Mia a watch to wear on her wrist. She was worried about the sea being too deep for Mia, but the watch would help.

Mia had a lot of fun. She swam and laughed, exploring the water. After an hour, Daddy said it was time to go back. Mia was a bit worried because she was having so much fun. 

Mummy and Daddy hugged her and said that it was OK to be worried about leaving the beach. They promised that they would come back another day for Mia to swim again. 

Mia knew that everything was all right. She was relieved and happy that she'd be able to swim again soon. The watch that Mummy had given her was still on her wrist and she was sure that it would remind her of the joy of swimming.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Jin and Ken. They were playing together in the field. Suddenly, Jin saw a pool. He pointed to it and shouted, "Look, Ken! A pool!"

Ken ran to the pool and looked inside. He said, "It's empty. What shall we do with it?"

Jin thought and then he said, "I know! Let's show our friends the empty pool!"

So the two friends ran to their friends' house. They showed them the empty pool. The friends were not impressed.

At this, Jin and Ken had a conflict. Jin said, "Let's fill the pool!"
Ken said, "Nope, I think it will be too much trouble."

In the end, Jin and Ken decided to forget about the empty pool and play in the field again. They had lots of fun together and eventually forgot all about the empty pool.

Once upon a time there was a quiet attic. Inside the attic were two sisters. The older sister, named Emma, was always in charge. 

One day while they were in the attic, Emma said to her younger sister, Lily. "Let's paint the walls of the attic!" Lily grinned, she had never painted before. 

Emma gave Lily a pot of bright green paint and a brush. "Paint the wall! Go on! Be brave!"

Lily held the brush and took a deep breath. She dipped the brush into the pot of paint and started painting. She painted little circles, big circles and even triangles until the whole wall was covered in bright green. 

When she finished painting, Lily looked around the attic. It was so quiet and even more wonderful with the walls painted green.

Once upon a time there was a big monster, he was so big that he filled all the sky. He roared so loud that the ground shook when he roared. He looked around and saw many people playing hockey. He liked the sound of the hockey sticks and wanted to try it. 

He came down from the sky and walked closer. The people playing hockey stopped and stared at the big monster. He looked so wide and the kids were scared. The monster said in a gentle voice, "Can I try hockey too?".

The kids were brave and said yes. So the monster grabbed a hockey stick, smiled and said, "Thank you!" He hit the hockey and it went so far and made a loud sound when it hit the ground. The kids couldn't believe it, they laughed and cheered. He was so happy he roared with joy. 

The kids and the monster played hockey together until the sun went down. They had lot of fun! They said goodbye and the monster rose up to the sky and waved. Finally, he roared one last time over the kids and flew away.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to explore the world. One day she decided to go for a walk and explore a new space for the first time. The space was a large park filled with delicate flowers and brightly coloured butterflies. She quickly noticed a man and a woman picking flowers from the bushes and she approached them with curiosity.

The little girl asked "What are you doing?".
The man replied "We are picking these flowers to include them in our garden, so we can enjoy them for a long time".
The little girl thought about the man's words and said "I like exploring different spaces and I think it is important to be careful with the things we pick, so we can enjoy them for a long time". 

The couple thanked the little girl for her words as they had never thought of this before. From then on they carefully picked the delicate flowers and decided to explore more spaces and appreciate the beauty around them.

The moral of the story is to always appreciate what we have and to be careful not to damage delicate things when exploring new spaces.

Lisa and Billy were playing in the backyard one day. Billy was sad and he started to complain.

Lisa said, "What's wrong, Billy?".

Billy said, "I want a pet, but my dad says we can't have one".

Lisa said, "That's too bad". She then had an incredible idea. She said, "We can find a bird in a cage".

Billy said, "Where can we find one?".

Lisa said, "Let's go to the park. I bet some people are selling birds there".

So the two of them went to the park, and sure enough there were people selling bird cages. Billy was so excited and he picked out the biggest one. It had an incredible songbird inside.

Billy was happy and he no longer had to complain. He had a pet of his very own.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sadie. She was three years old and loved to play with her toys in the park. One day, while she was playing in the park, she saw a van.

"Oh, wow!" Sadie said. "I want to hold the van!" She ran over to the van and started to touch it.

Sadie's mom saw what she was doing and said, "No, Sadie! That van isn't yours. You can't hold it."

Sadie put her hands behind her back and looked at the ground. She felt very guilty. Her mom said, "It's okay, Sadie. We'll find you another van."

Sadie looked up with a big smile on her face. She was so happy that her mom wasn't mad at her. Her mom hugged her and said, "It's important to follow the rules, Sadie. Otherwise, we'll both feel guilty."

Sadie nodded her head and said, "Okay, Mom. I won't hold the van anymore." From then on, Sadie followed the rules and never touched anyone else's things without permission.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Sam and Trudy. They lived in a town with a rich, beautiful structure. Every day, Trudy and Sam would go and visit the structure.

One day, the structure was gone. Trudy was very sad. She looked all over town, but it was nowhere to be seen.

She said to Sam, "What happened to our structure?" 

Sam said, "I don't know, but I really miss it."

Trudy said, "Me too! Let's look around and see if we can find it."

They searched all over town, but they could not find it. Trudy felt so sad.

Trudy said, "I wish we could find our structure, I miss it so much!"

But even though they looked and looked, they could not find their rich, beautiful structure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Clara. She had long blonde hair and a great big smile.

One day, Clara was outside playing in her garden when she found a handle. She picked it up and wondered what it might belong to. 

Suddenly, a voice called out to her. 

"Clara, where did you find that handle?" Clara looked up and saw a tall man with a frown on his face. 

"I found it in the garden," Clara said. 

"That's terrible!" the man said. "That handle belongs to my axe. I must have dropped it!" 

The man thanked Clara for finding his handle and took it back to his house. Clara was happy she had been able to help someone, and glad that the handle belonged to someone.

Billy was a happy boy. He loved pushing things. One day, he saw an avocado. It was big, green and bumpy. He wanted to push the avocado, so he did! He pushed it with all his might. Suddenly, something amazing happened. The avocado turned pink! He kept pushing and pushing, and the avocado kept turning pinker and pinker. Billy was so excited! He had changed the avocado to his favorite color - pink!

Once there was a rabbit who was hopping through the meadow. He stopped when he saw a bean. He wanted to eat it, but then he heard a voice. It was an old owl who was perched on the branch of a nearby tree.

"Don't eat that bean, little rabbit," the owl warned.

But the rabbit was hungry and very tempted. So he picked up the bean and was about to eat it, when the owl spoke again.

"Lucky for you, rabbit," the owl said. "That bean is magical. If you eat it, you'll stay a rabbit forever and never grow. Is that what you really want?"

The rabbit shook his head. He didn't want to stay a little rabbit forever. The owl was right. He was very lucky the owl had warned him. So the rabbit hopped away without eating the bean.

The moral of the story is: it is always important to listen to warnings and take advice from wise people. They just might save you from making a big mistake.

Once there was a young girl named Sandy. She liked to go to the park every day and play with her friends. One day, when Sandy was playing in the park, she saw a man who was sleeping on a bench. She decided to be kind and make him a sandwich. 

Sandy made a sandwich and was about to give it to the man. But before she could do so, he woke up and began to yell and disturb everyone. He was very angry and started throwing things around. 

Sandy was scared and quickly ran away. Even though she had tried to do something nice for the man, he was so mad that he disturbed the peace. Sandy learned a valuable lesson that day: being too nice can sometimes get you into trouble.

Once upon a time, there was an old man who lived in a big house. One day, he was walking around his garden and he saw a filthy skin on the floor. He was very surprised and he wanted to pick it up, but it was heavy and he couldn't lift it. So he just bent down and gave it a push, and it dropped into the pond!

The pond got much dirtier with the filthy skin, and the old man was very angry. He wanted to get it out, but it was so heavy! He got a big stick and tried to fish it out, but it just wouldn't come. So he just watched, and the skin slowly sank to the bottom.

But then something miraculous happened! After a few weeks, the filthy skin disappeared! The old man couldn't believe it, and he wondered what had happened. He thought and he thought, until he realized the answer: The skin had rotted away! 

The old man was happy that the filthy skin was gone and he was careful to never drop anything else into the pond again.

One day, Peter and his Grandma decided to go on a walk in the park. It was a very sunny day and Peter was excited to explore all of the sights. 

As they made their way through the park, Peter noticed something unusual. He saw a large muscle on the ground. 

"What is that?" asked Peter. 

"I'm not sure," replied Grandma. "Let's go have a closer look."

When they approached the muscle, they noticed it was twitching. 

"I guess it's alive!" exclaimed Peter. 

Grandma smiled and nodded. "Let's move away and let it rest. It must be very tired."

They watched the muscle carefully until it disappeared in the distance. Peter had seen something unusual on his walk.

Little Sammy was walking in the garden one day. He noticed a wide sunflower and smiled. He took a deep breath and said to it, "Hello sunflower. I surrender to you." He ran his hands through its petals and admired its beauty. 

Suddenly, the sunflower started to move. Sammy's eyes widened in amazement. "What are you doing?" He asked curiously.

The sunflower said, "I'm surrendering right back to you." Sammy laughed and ran around the garden. He was so excited.

Every day Sammy ran to the garden to see the wide sunflower. They shared stories, laughed, and enjoyed each other's company. They were the best of friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Clara. She was three years old and she loved to explore the world around her.

One day, Clara was playing in a park near her house when she saw a big white bird. It had a long neck and a beak. She was very curious and asked the bird, â€œWhat are you?â€

The bird replied, â€œI am a crane.â€

Clara was so excited. She asked the crane, â€œCan I take you flying?â€ The crane smiled and replied, â€œYes, letâ€™s go!â€

So, Clara and the crane flew into the sky. It was very chilly and there were icy clouds everywhere. Clara was so happy she couldnâ€™t stop laughing.

After a while the crane said, â€œItâ€™s getting too cold for me, so I need to go now.â€ â€œOkay,â€ replied Clara sadly. â€œFly safely." 

The crane smiled and flew away. Clara waved goodbye and went home. She felt very happy and cozy inside.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who lived in a small house. She was very excited because it was dinner time. She went to the kitchen and asked her mom what dinner was.

Her mom said, "We are having pasta tonight!" 

The little girl was so excited that she started to insist that dinner should be pasta.

But her mom said that she was going to have something else. The little girl got angry and insisted that dinner should only be pasta.

Her mom looked at her and said, "Listen, you can't always get what you want. Insisting too much can be broken."

The little girl understood what her mom was saying and realised that it was important to be patient and understand that sometimes things don't go the way we want. That night, she learned that in life it is important to be patient and understand that we can't always get what we want.

One day, a little girl was feeling very eager. She ran over to her special toy box and took out a plate. Then she placed it on the floor and began to roll it around. Each time it rolled, it made funny noises which made the little girl giggle. She kept rolling the plate around for a very long time. She was having so much fun!
